heuristics.rule: If H-1B lottery fails, exhaust visa alternatives in priority order before resorting to consultancy/ICC routes
heuristics.condition: When H-1B lottery is not selected and the person needs to maintain US work authorization
heuristics.action: Evaluate O-1, L-1, EB-1/EB-2 direct green card, exempt-employer H-1B, STEM OPT extension, or J-1 before engaging a consultancy sponsorship arrangement
heuristics.because: The post explicitly lists 10 alternatives with pros/cons, and the consultancy route is characterized as high-risk with exploitative conditions by the Indian worker's firsthand account

heuristics.rule: Retain all enrollment documentation if using CPT to maintain F-1 status while re-entering H-1B lottery
heuristics.condition: When using CPT as a bridge strategy to re-attempt H-1B in subsequent years
heuristics.action: Keep I-20s, transcripts, assignments, tuition payment receipts, transportation records, and course syllabi
heuristics.because: The post explicitly warns that CPT-based applicants should be prepared for RFE and need these documents as evidence of genuine enrollment

heuristics.rule: Target cap-exempt employers (universities, affiliated nonprofits, government research institutions) if you need H-1B without lottery exposure
heuristics.condition: When H-1B lottery odds are unacceptable and the person can accept a role at a qualifying institution
heuristics.action: Seek positions at universities (all roles, not just faculty), university-affiliated nonprofits, nonprofit research orgs, or government research orgs
heuristics.because: The post explicitly states these employers can file H-1B at any time, without cap or lottery, effective immediately upon approval

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Consultancy-based H-1B sponsorship arrangements require candidates to have real experience and self-sufficient interviewing ability; without it, this route is closed. With it, hourly rate and take-home compensation vary substantially.
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count years of experience on actual projects; assess ability to pass technical interviews independently without coaching or resume fabrication

decision_factors.why_it_matters: The consultancy model can delay first payment by 3-4 months due to invoice cycles (monthly billing + 45-day vendor payment cycle + 15-day processing). Without savings, the person faces severe financial distress.
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate whether you can cover 4-5 months of US living expenses from personal savings before committing to a consultancy-sponsored arrival

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Consultancy-based bulk lottery sponsorship exists across many fields (IT, accounting, sales, legal, bioinfo, supply chain, civil engineering), not just software — broadening or narrowing options depending on the person's industry
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research whether your specific field has an active consultancy/contract staffing ecosystem in the US

decision_factors.factor: Eligibility for O-1 or EB-1 direct path
decision_factors.why_it_matters: These routes bypass the lottery entirely with no annual cap, but require evidence of extraordinary ability — available to fewer people but dramatically better terms
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether you have: major awards, media coverage, high-impact publications, judging roles, or critical organizational roles that meet USCIS criteria

decision_factors.why_it_matters: J-1 visa holders subject to the two-year rule must obtain a waiver (4-6 month process) before applying for H-1B, adding significant delay
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check DS-2019 and program type to determine if two-year rule applies; factor in waiver processing time if planning J-1 as a bridge

hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: First paycheck may not arrive for 3-4 months after joining a client site due to cascading invoice cycles (monthly billing → 45-day vendor payment → 15-day consultancy processing). Living costs, LCA amendment fees (~$1200 per location change), and no employer-covered relocation compound rapidly into $10,000+ out-of-pocket before any income arrives.
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Anyone who arrives in the US with limited savings relying on the consultancy's promise of rapid project placement

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Using CPT to maintain F-1 status and re-attempt H-1B lottery
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Exposes the applicant to RFE scrutiny in future H-1B filings; requires genuine course attendance and documentation burden on top of full-time work; tuition is an additional cost; re-entry to the US carries risk
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: People treating CPT as a paperwork formality rather than genuine enrollment, or those with low academic backgrounds

hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: If you later want to move to a private-sector employer subject to the cap, you re-enter the lottery and lose cap-exempt protection — the H-1B does not transfer cap-exempt status
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: People using cap-exempt employment as a long-term career strategy rather than a temporary bridge

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: H-4 EAD as work authorization while spouse holds H-1B
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: H-4 EAD work authorization only becomes available after the H-1B holder's employment-based green card has reached a specific stage (I-140 approved or in 6th-year extension) — not available immediately upon marriage
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Couples where the H-4 spouse plans to work immediately, not understanding the prerequisite conditions

failure_patterns.pattern: Arriving in the US via consultancy sponsorship without adequate savings, trusting the '15-day project placement' promise
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Optimism bias and the consultancy's sales framing ('we'll take care of everything, just come') creates an underestimation of actual time-to-first-paycheck
failure_patterns.consequence: Financial distress for 3-5 months: no income, out-of-pocket LCA amendment costs, no health insurance, no car, substandard shared housing — total cash outflow of $20,000-$30,000 before breaking even
warning_signs: Consultancy promises project placement within 15 days
Consultancy offers housing as part of the arrangement
No clarity provided on payment cycle or when first paycheck arrives

failure_patterns.pattern: Treating CPT enrollment as a paperwork formality rather than genuine coursework
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Students are focused on maintaining work authorization and view the course requirement as bureaucratic overhead, not understanding USCIS scrutiny of CPT patterns
failure_patterns.consequence: H-1B RFE in subsequent year requiring extensive documentation that was never collected; potential status violation if enrollment was not genuine
warning_signs: Student selects school primarily for CPT access, not academic quality
Student does not attend class or retain course materials
Student cannot produce transcripts, assignments, or tuition receipts

failure_patterns.pattern: Underestimating the LCA amendment cost as a recurring expense when changing client locations under consultancy H-1B
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Workers focus on the hourly rate and the 80/20 or 70/30 split, failing to account for the $1,200 per-location amendment fee that recurs every time the client or work location changes
failure_patterns.consequence: Repeated unexpected out-of-pocket costs eroding effective take-home pay, especially for contractors who rotate client sites frequently
warning_signs: Consultancy does not proactively disclose amendment fees at time of offer
Worker is placed in a contract role that involves frequent client site changes

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have at least 1-2 years of real, verifiable project experience and can you pass technical interviews independently?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines eligibility for consultancy-based bulk lottery sponsorship — these companies require genuine experience and interviewing ability, unlike training-based ICCs
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Assess your financial runway: can you cover 4-5 months of US living expenses before your first paycheck?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Consultancy route is not viable; focus on employer-sponsored paths, OPT extension, or further education

diagnostic_questions.question: Does your current or target employer qualify as cap-exempt (university, university-affiliated nonprofit, government research org)?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: If yes, H-1B can be filed at any time without lottery — fundamentally changes the urgency and strategy of H-1B planning
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Negotiate directly with that employer for H-1B sponsorship outside the lottery cycle
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Must plan around the annual April lottery window and evaluate bridge visa options for gap years

diagnostic_questions.question: If considering J-1 as an alternative, are you subject to the two-year home residency requirement?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether J-1 is a viable bridge strategy or adds a 4-6 month waiver process before any H-1B can be filed
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Factor in J-1 waiver timeline (4-6 months) into your overall status planning; J-1 may not be a clean bridge
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: J-1 as trainee may be a viable bridge if you can find a DS-2019-issuing employer

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have documented evidence of extraordinary ability — major awards, significant media coverage, judging roles, critical organizational contributions?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether O-1 or EB-1A is a realistic alternative to H-1B, bypassing the lottery entirely
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Consult an immigration attorney to assess O-1 or EB-1A eligibility — these paths have no cap and no lottery
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: O-1/EB-1A are unlikely viable; focus on H-1B lottery, cap-exempt employers, or EB-2/EB-3 with employer support

industry_realities.common_belief: Consultancy-based H-1B sponsorship (ICC/body shop) is primarily a phenomenon in the software/IT industry
industry_realities.actual_reality: According to the post, consultancy-based bulk lottery sponsorship exists across accounting, sales, legal, bioinformatics, supply chain, civil engineering, and other contract-staffing industries — it is structurally similar to what Indian workers call 'consultancy' and is standard practice in any field that uses contract workers
industry_realities.implication: Workers in non-IT fields should be aware this model exists in their industry and evaluate the same risks (payment delays, exploitative splits, amendment costs)

industry_realities.common_belief: The consultancy will cover your expenses and get you placed quickly after you arrive in the US
industry_realities.actual_reality: Consultancies typically cover only a token portion of shared housing; all other expenses (SIM, SSN, transportation, food, LCA amendments) are borne by the worker. First paycheck routinely arrives 3-4 months after joining due to cascading billing cycles, not the implied 1-2 months.
industry_realities.implication: Anyone relying on consultancy support must arrive with substantial personal savings ($10,000-$15,000 minimum) to survive the gap period

industry_realities.common_belief: Transferring an existing project from one ICC to another ICC that sponsored your H-1B is a gray area that 'nobody enforces'
industry_realities.actual_reality: The post explicitly flags this as illegal — transferring a project from a previous ICC to the new H-1B sponsor is a violation, even if enforcement is rare. The legal path requires finding a genuinely new project.
industry_realities.implication: Workers who transfer projects to their new H-1B sponsor are taking on legal risk; they should source new projects to remain fully compliant

industry_realities.common_belief: H-4 visa holders can work as soon as their spouse gets H-1B status
industry_realities.actual_reality: H-4 EAD work authorization requires the H-1B principal to have reached a specific green card milestone (approved I-140 or in 6th-year H-1B extension) — it is not automatically available at H-1B approval
industry_realities.implication: Couples planning around H-4 work authorization need to map the H-1B holder's green card timeline before assuming the H-4 spouse can work

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Treats lottery failure as a binary dead end — either find another lottery attempt or give up on the US; defaults to the most immediately available option (consultancy sponsorship) without evaluating alternatives
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Immediately maps all alternative visa pathways (O-1, L-1, J-1, cap-exempt H-1B, EB-1/EB-2 direct, STEM OPT extension, spouse visa) and evaluates each against their specific profile before deciding
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Defaulting to consultancy sponsorship without evaluation exposes the person to 3-4 months of financial hardship and exploitative contract terms that could have been avoided with a better-matched alternative

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Focuses on the advertised hourly rate and the 80/20 split; accepts verbal promises about project placement speed and housing support at face value
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Calculates true take-home after the split AND recurring amendment fees; models time-to-first-paycheck based on actual billing cycles (monthly invoice + 45-day vendor payment + 15-day processing); verifies savings adequacy before committing
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: The naive calculation makes the arrangement look viable; the informed calculation often reveals a 3-5 month cash-negative period that is financially dangerous without sufficient reserves

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Views CPT purely as a work authorization mechanism; selects school for CPT access and treats coursework as administrative overhead
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Understands CPT creates RFE exposure in future H-1B filings; treats enrollment as genuine and proactively collects all documentation (I-20s, transcripts, assignments, tuition receipts) from day one
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Failure to document genuine enrollment can result in H-1B denial via RFE and potential retrospective status violations

community_misconceptions.misconception: If you use CPT to stay in the US after H-1B lottery failure, your next H-1B application will be treated the same as any other applicant
community_misconceptions.why_believed: CPT is a legitimate F-1 benefit and the connection between CPT usage and increased H-1B scrutiny is not widely publicized
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: USCIS may issue an RFE for H-1B applicants who used CPT, requiring extensive documentation proving the CPT enrollment was genuine (I-20, transcripts, assignments, syllabi, tuition payments, transportation records)
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Applicants who treated CPT as a formality and did not retain documentation may have their H-1B denied or delayed due to inability to respond to RFE

community_misconceptions.misconception: The consultancy model is unique to the Indian IT community and doesn't affect other nationalities or industries
community_misconceptions.why_believed: Most visible discussions of ICCs and body shops in Chinese-language communities focus on Indian-run IT consultancies, creating a perception of narrow demographic scope
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: Consultancy-based contract staffing and bulk H-1B sponsorship exists across all contract-heavy industries (accounting, legal, bioinfo, supply chain, civil engineering, sales) and is not limited to any nationality or field
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Workers in non-IT fields may walk into exploitative consultancy arrangements without recognizing the pattern because they don't associate the warning signs with their industry

community_misconceptions.misconception: H-4 visa holders can work in the US as soon as their H-1B spouse's petition is approved
community_misconceptions.why_believed: People conflate H-4 status (granted at H-1B approval) with H-4 EAD (work authorization), which has different and more restrictive eligibility requirements
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: H-4 EAD requires the H-1B principal to have an approved I-140 or to be in a 6th-year H-1B extension — work authorization is not automatic at H-1B approval
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: H-4 holders who begin working without EAD authorization are working illegally; couples who planned financially around dual income may face an unexpected gap

real_case_outcomes.situation: Indian software developer with 11 years of experience, H-1B sponsored by a consultancy firm, arrived in the US with promise of housing and project placement within 15 days
real_case_outcomes.decision: Accepted the consultancy's terms, paid $4,000 in H-1B fees, booked a flight, arrived expecting to be self-sufficient within 1-2 months
real_case_outcomes.outcome: Found a project in 3 weeks but SSN delays pushed start date to 1.5 months post-arrival. Consultancy did not pay until 3-4 months after joining due to monthly billing + 45-day vendor cycle + 15-day processing. Forced to pay $1,200 LCA amendment fee upon client location change. Lived in overcrowded shared housing. No health insurance, no car, severe financial and emotional stress. Total out-of-pocket before earning: ~$30,000 USD including opportunity cost.
real_case_outcomes.lesson: The consultancy model structurally delays income by 3-4 months while front-loading all financial risk onto the worker. Anyone entering this arrangement must have $15,000-$30,000 in savings and must not rely on consultancy promises of fast placement or expense coverage. The 80/20 split sounds favorable but recurring amendment fees and payment delays erode actual compensation significantly.

psychological_barriers.trigger: H-1B lottery failure — person asks 'what do I do now?' with urgency, often framing it as an either/or between consultancy sponsorship and leaving the US
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Loss aversion and tunnel vision — the person has invested years in building a US career and frames any path that keeps them in the US as acceptable, without evaluating the actual costs of each path
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Jumps to the first available option (consultancy sponsorship) without comparing alternatives; accepts consultancy promises at face value because the alternative (leaving) feels catastrophic
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe: lottery failure is not a binary between 'consultancy' and 'leaving' — map all 10 alternatives first, then evaluate each against your specific profile. The consultancy route often costs more (financially and emotionally) than the alternatives appear to.

psychological_barriers.trigger: Person is already committed to a consultancy arrangement and is asking about when they'll get paid or how the process works
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Sunk cost fallacy — having already paid fees, booked flights, and arrived in the US, the person is psychologically committed and seeks reassurance rather than honest evaluation
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Asks narrow tactical questions ('when will I get paid?') rather than stepping back to evaluate whether the arrangement is viable given their savings; dismisses red flags as temporary
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Surface the full payment timeline math explicitly: monthly billing + 45-day vendor cycle + 15-day processing = 3-4 months minimum. Ask: 'Do you have enough savings to cover that entire period plus unexpected costs like LCA amendments?' Make the financial model concrete before they're trapped.

psychological_barriers.trigger: Person compares the consultancy worker's eventual $100K+ salary to current situation and finds it aspirational, minimizing the hardship story
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Survivorship bias and outcome bias — the person focuses on the eventual income outcome and discounts the process costs (financial, emotional, health, family separation)
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Comments like 'sounds worth it to me, $10K-$18K take-home a year is great' without accounting for the $30K upfront cost, 4-5 months of zero income, health risk from no insurance, and sustained emotional distress
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Make the full cost-benefit calculation explicit: total investment ($30K+), months of negative cash flow, health insurance gap, opportunity cost of foregone India income, and the 'treated like shit' quality-of-life dimension. Ask: 'Would you accept a job that required a $30K loan, no pay for 4 months, no health insurance, and exploitative working conditions to start?'

reframing_moves.original_framing: H-1B lottery failed — how do I get an H-1B through a consultancy?
reframing_moves.reframe: H-1B lottery failure is not the end of your US career path — there are 10 structurally different alternatives, each with different eligibility requirements, costs, and risk profiles. The consultancy route is one of the worst options for most people.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts from a single-path scarcity mindset to a portfolio evaluation mindset, reducing the psychological pressure that makes people accept bad consultancy terms
reframing_moves.example_language: Plan A行不通，不是还有Plan B、Plan C、Plan D排队等着你嘛 ('If Plan A doesn't work, aren't Plan B, C, and D lined up waiting for you?')

reframing_moves.original_framing: Is the consultancy H-1B route worth it given the eventual salary?
reframing_moves.reframe: The question is not whether the eventual salary is good — it's whether the total cost of getting there (fees, months without pay, amendment costs, health risk, emotional toll, family separation) justifies the path compared to alternatives
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts from outcome anchoring (focusing only on the destination salary) to full lifecycle cost accounting, revealing that the consultancy path often costs $30K+ before any income arrives
reframing_moves.example_language: 至于大家有没有觉得这位印度老哥被自己人坑了活的很惨，还是觉着他非但没有被退休，反而还能一年能拿10几万美金过的很爽…就请自行判断 ('Whether you think this Indian guy was exploited and miserable, or that he's doing well earning $100K+ — judge for yourself')
